correctness.rationale: The source exact count-block flat spectra determine their squared Frobenius masses and spectral norms. Although count blocks with a shared row or column are not mutually Schmidt-orthogonal, their Frobenius inner products are zero; low-count difference cutoff therefore retains exactly the binomial mass, and has rank at most a polynomial times 2^(b sqrt(t)). The complementary high-difference operator norm is at most t(t+1)2^(-b sqrt(t)/2) by triangle inequality. Exact Eckart–Young dual bounds sandwich every best-r retained weight; binomial CLT yields half-normal CDF erf(b) and continuity yields the exact quantile coefficient. Verified the source’s critical nonstandard finite-time spectra via 2736 independent exact-integer assertions from explicit folded gate; limits, source dependencies and nonclaims are stated.

Exactly determining the full retained squared-weight curve and its inverse accuracy-rank constant is a natural and useful simulation-complexity benchmark, distinguishing exponentially different truncation budgets at different fidelity levels.
